words.sense: view that moral categories do not apply or lack real meaning
words.connotation: philosophical; can sound dismissive of moral evaluation
misconceptions: Assuming rejecting universal rules rejects morality itself.
Treating context-dependent moral rules as no rules at all.

words.sense: view that judgments of right and wrong depend on culture or perspective
words.connotation: context-sensitive; may stress tolerance of difference
misconceptions: Treating doubts about moral labels as a debate over cultures.

semantic_axes.description: Amoralism denies meaningful moral judgments, whereas relativism accepts judgments but makes their standards dependent on perspective or culture.

edges.boundary_rule: Amoralism denies meaningful moral judgments, whereas relativism accepts judgments but makes their standards dependent on perspective or culture.

misconceptions.M1: Assuming rejecting universal rules rejects morality itself.
misconceptions.M2: Treating doubts about moral labels as a debate over cultures.
misconceptions.M3: Treating context-dependent moral rules as no rules at all.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Nila's position in the class debate?

beats.text: Nila says calling a classmate good or bad is no more meaningful than calling a chair guilty.
beats.decisive_clue: she treats moral labels as meaningless
beats.reason: She treats moral labels as meaningless is the evidence for amoralism.

beats.text: She applies that view even when everyone in the room agrees an action caused harm.
beats.decisive_clue: moral labels remain meaningless even with agreement
beats.reason: Agreement about harm does not make right-and-wrong labels meaningful in her view.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: she treats moral labels as meaningless.
chains.feedback_deep: Amoralism denies that moral judgments have meaningful application. Relativism would still allow judgments based on a group or perspective. Nila rejects the category itself, even when a group agrees.
chains.contrast_rule: Amoralism dismisses moral judgment; relativism changes whose standard is used.

hints.attention: Ask whether any moral standard survives, and where it comes from.

hints.contrast: Amoralism dismisses moral judgment; relativism changes whose standard is used.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Omar's argument at dinner?

beats.text: Omar says a duty in one household may be optional in another, because families develop different rules.
beats.decisive_clue: he grounds duties in each household’s standards
beats.reason: He grounds duties in each household’s standards is the evidence for relativism.

beats.text: He adds that each household can still fairly judge its members against its own expectations.
beats.decisive_clue: he preserves standards within each household
beats.reason: The added qualification strengthens the context-dependent standard rather than abandoning judgment.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: he preserves standards within each household.
chains.feedback_deep: Relativism lets standards vary by setting; it does not mean nobody can act wrongly. Omar allows each family to hold members to its own rules.
chains.contrast_rule: Amoralism dismisses moral judgment; relativism changes whose standard is used.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Mei's view in her forum post?

beats.text: Mei first says that different gaming clubs have different ideas about fair play.
beats.reason: Different clubs apply different judgments is the evidence for relativism.

beats.text: She explains that no such rule carries any moral meaning, even for the club that created it.
beats.decisive_clue: she denies moral meaning even within a club
beats.reason: The new claim rejects moral judgment itself, not merely universal standards.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: she denies moral meaning even within a club.
chains.feedback_deep: The first claim fits relativism: judgments vary across clubs. Her clarification goes further and removes moral meaning even within a given group, which is amoralism.
chains.contrast_rule: Amoralism dismisses moral judgment; relativism changes whose standard is used.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Luis's claim at the meeting?

beats.text: Luis says no one can meaningfully call a neighbour morally better merely for following a rule.
beats.decisive_clue: he denies the validity of moral praise
beats.reason: He denies the validity of moral praise is the evidence for amoralism.

beats.text: His point is that praise and blame, not just punishments, lack any moral force.
beats.decisive_clue: he rejects moral praise and blame altogether
beats.reason: Including blame confirms that he rejects the whole category of moral evaluation.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: he rejects moral praise and blame altogether.
chains.feedback_deep: Amoralism concerns whether moral judgments apply at all. Luis denies both moral praise and blame rather than comparing the standards of different neighbourhoods.
chains.contrast_rule: Amoralism dismisses moral judgment; relativism changes whose standard is used.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Inez's opinion about rating sellers?

beats.text: Inez says a seller’s refusal to accept returns is fair in markets where that practice is understood, but unfair where returns are promised.
beats.decisive_clue: she judges fairness by agreed market norms
beats.reason: She judges fairness by agreed market norms is the evidence for relativism.

beats.text: Her post attracts five hundred responses and is pinned at the top of the shop forum.
beats.decisive_clue: the original dependence on local agreements is decisive
beats.reason: The number of responses changes the post’s visibility, not her context-dependent judgment.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: she judges fairness by agreed market norms.
chains.feedback_deep: Relativism lets judgments depend on accepted standards. Inez is applying each market’s expectations to the same practice; the popularity of her post changes nothing.
chains.contrast_rule: Amoralism dismisses moral judgment; relativism changes whose standard is used.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Ayaan's view of volunteer duties?

beats.text: Ayaan says refusing a weekend shift is judged selfish in one community but perfectly acceptable in another.
beats.decisive_clue: he makes judgment depend on community standards
beats.reason: He makes judgment depend on community standards is the evidence for relativism.

beats.text: He insists that each community must apply its own expectations rather than borrow someone else’s.
beats.decisive_clue: community standards still determine each judgment
beats.reason: Insisting that groups use their own standards reinforces, rather than removes, his original view.

chains.feedback_short: The deciding clue: he makes judgment depend on community standards.
chains.feedback_deep: Relativism makes moral evaluation depend on a perspective or culture. Ayaan does not deny the category of selfishness; he changes which community’s rules determine it.
chains.contrast_rule: Amoralism dismisses moral judgment; relativism changes whose standard is used.
